name: Soul Asylum
label: Twin/Tone
lede: Dave Pirner's band started as Loud Fast Rules, put out three records in 1986 for Twin/Tone, then took a ballad written on a napkin to No. 5 and a Grammy. After Karl Mueller died in 2005, Pirner kept the name going.

eras.title: A drummer who sings
eras.text: Dan Murphy talks Karl Mueller into bass, Dave Pirner won't leave the drum stool, and the trio plays as Loud Fast Rules. They put two songs on a cassette compilation and change the name before anyone signs them.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · EnterTheSoulAsylum: Biography · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: [[Dave Pirner|8849e71c-181b-444b-8cfb-09445e6231d4]] sings from behind the drums in Loud Fast Rules
years.p: Guitarist [[Dan Murphy|06806bee-5233-4c4e-b644-2243620278db]] and bassist [[Karl Mueller|dde72be5-d90f-4390-b441-bb8288ec0404]] complete a trio whose name is the entire plan. Pirner won't leave the kit for the first year.
years.xp:
Murphy told Perfect Sound Forever he first saw Pirner's band at Zoogy's around 1981, and that the trio came together within four weeks. Mueller was back from England a punk convert, but didn't play an instrument. Murphy: "I said, 'You're going to play bass.' We brought like this green Epiphone bass that some guy painted with house paint."

Of Pirner on drums: "He insisted on being our drummer for the first year." Murphy says he eventually talked Pirner off the stool to focus on singing and songwriting. Wikipedia lists Pat Morley as an original drummer, which doesn't sit easily with Murphy's account.

years.src: Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: Barefoot and Pregnant is the first tape with their songs on it
years.p: Loud Fast Rules put two songs on a Reflex Records cassette compilation, then turn up on a second one, Kitten, billed as Proud Crass Fools.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Kitten was recorded live at Goofy's Upper Deck, with the band's name on the sleeve as Proud Crass Fools. Both tapes were local Reflex Records releases.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum · EnterTheSoulAsylum: Biography
years.h: A Pirner song title becomes the band's new name
years.p: Pirner moves to rhythm guitar and Pat Morley takes the drums as Loud Fast Rules turns into Soul Asylum.
years.xp: Murphy told Perfect Sound Forever: "Dave had a song called Soul Asylum that none of us really loved, but that was a cool title." He says the label suggested the change. Wikipedia dates the rename to 1983, and the band's own site agrees.

eras.title: Twin/Tone, and Bob Mould's schedule
eras.text: The label that already has the Replacements signs a band with no album. Hüsker Dü's Bob Mould produces two of their records on budgets of a few thousand dollars, and the drummer chair changes hands.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: Twin/Tone Records
years.h: Peter Jesperson signs a band with no album to Twin/Tone
years.p: Jesperson co-founded the Minneapolis label in 1977, and it's already home to [[The Replacements|dc0d05ce-2f47-4962-b4fa-8631a0a51987]]. Soul Asylum haven't released a record yet.
years.xp:
Murphy to Perfect Sound Forever: "That was bigger than getting signed at Columbia or Big Six, because they're the only game in town." He also says: "I have never gotten a single check from Twin/Tone in my life, a royalty check. Ever."

Twin/Tone Records was founded in 1977 by Jesperson, Charley Hallman and Paul Stark, and by 1984 had put out 41 records with three paid staff, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: Say What You Will · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum · Twin/Tone Digital: Soul Asylum
years.h: [[Bob Mould|d7f5305a-15fc-4af4-a61b-f6f45510cc8f]] skips day one of Say What You Will
years.p: Murphy says the debut was made for about $4,000 and Mould, the producer, didn't show on the first day. That year Karl Mueller sells the band's Chevrolet pickup to buy a bigger Dodge van for the tours.
years.xp:
Murphy to Perfect Sound Forever: "The first day of our record, he didn't even show up, so say what you will." On the budget: "I made those records for 4000 bucks. Not because I wanted to, but because I was told to." Wikipedia credits Blake Gumprecht as co-producer and Steve Fjelstad as engineer.

The original pressing moved 6,738 vinyl copies and 2,639 cassettes, per Wikipedia. The 1988 CD reissue added five unreleased tracks and became Say What You Will, Clarence...Karl Sold the Truck. Trouser Press hears the record as the end of the band's "hardcore slop phase".

years.h: Grant Young takes the drum stool from Pat Morley
years.p: Morley quits after the first record. Young settles in and stays until 1995.

eras.title: 112 shows and three records
eras.text: A record in January, a cassette in June, another album in November, and a van in between. Opening for Hüsker Dü and headlining around First Avenue make them a working band with nothing left in the tank.

years.src: Wikipedia: Made to Be Broken · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: Mould produces again on Made to Be Broken, Young's first record
years.p: Recorded in 1985 and out on January 18, it's the first of three Soul Asylum releases in 1986.
years.xp: Trouser Press calls it "an essential Soul Asylum LP" and points to "raging dual vocals and interwoven guitar work" between Pirner and Murphy, with "Tied to the Tracks" and "Ship of Fools" as highlights. The Spin Alternative Record Guide credits Young's "off-kilter, rhythmic swerve".

years.cap: Dave Pirner, Dan Murphy, Karl Mueller and Grant Young
years.src: EnterTheSoulAsylum: 1986 shows · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: Soul Asylum open for Hüsker Dü on the Flip Your Wig tour
years.p: La Crosse, Madison, Milwaukee and Chicago in January, then Boston, New York, Philadelphia and Athens, Georgia, for the band whose singer, Bob Mould, produced their first two records.
years.xp: The fan-run EnterTheSoulAsylum show archive lists the Hüsker Dü dates across January and February 1986. By then Mould had produced both of Soul Asylum's Twin/Tone albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Time's Incinerator · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: Cassette-only Time's Incinerator sweeps up outtakes and a James Brown cover
years.p: Twin/Tone puts outtakes, B-sides and Loud Fast Rules-era demos on tape alone, with the James Brown cover credited to Mueller.
years.xp: The last track on side two is an improvised live set by Madison hardcore band Mecht Mensch, recorded when a shared bill hit technical trouble. Trouser Press describes the tape as outtakes, covers and live material from 1980 to 1986. The Spin Alternative Record Guide gave it 5/10.

years.cap: Dan Murphy practicing at the band's studio on Nicollet Avenue, South Minneapolis, May 1986
years.src: EnterTheSoulAsylum: 1986 shows
yt: Crashing Down, live at The Rat, Boston, 1987
years.h: TSOL cancels, so Soul Asylum play before Bad Brains
years.p: At First Avenue on October 20, the fan-run show archive says the night ends with the drummer alone on stage.
years.xp: The same archive counts 112 Soul Asylum shows in 1986, coast to coast. On May 20 the band won Best Garage Band at the Minnesota Music Awards alongside Hüsker Dü, and the archive's diary entry calls Pirner's acceptance speech "crazy".

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: While You Were Out · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: Two months between tours is all While You Were Out gets
years.p: Chris Osgood produces the third release of 1986. Robert Christgau gives it a B+; Trouser Press hears "thin, messy production".
years.xp:
Murphy told Perfect Sound Forever the record was rushed in two months while the band was touring, and that the result disappointed them. The New York Times, quoted on Wikipedia, called the sound "explosive speed-rock in jubilant major keys".

The Wildhearts covered "The Judge" in 1992, and Automatic 7 later recorded "Closer to the Stars".

eras.title: The A&M detour
eras.text: A major label signs the band, then the A&R man who championed them leaves before the first record ships. Twin/Tone still gets one more record out, with its own logo on a Herb Alpert parody.

years.cap: Dave Pirner, Dan Murphy, Karl Mueller and Grant Young, 1988
years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: Hang Time · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
yt: Sometime To Return, on Mouth to Mouth, Dec 6, 1988
years.h: A&M's champion leaves four weeks before Hang Time ships
years.p: [[Ed Stasium|23336099-24e0-40e7-af6d-a224bcdb4e41]] and [[Lenny Kaye|47455aa4-c71e-4662-a775-33b81fcf0a37]] produce the major-label debut. Murphy says A&M's support faded when A&R man Steve Ralbovsky walked out the door.
years.xp:
Murphy's own "Cartoon" is one of three singles, with "Marionette" and "Little Too Clean". Trouser Press credits the record with "unprecedented sonic excellence"; Robert Christgau gave it a B-.

Murphy also says Columbia's Donnie Ienner later signed the band after hearing a demo that included "Runaway Train".

years.src: Wikipedia: Clam Dip & Other Delights · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: Mueller sits in whipped cream and seafood for Clam Dip
years.p: The cover parodies Herb Alpert's Whipped Cream & Other Delights as a nod to the band's new label, A&M, with Twin/Tone's logo where A&M's would go.
years.xp:
Mueller replaced the original cover's model and, per Wikipedia, spent hours in a mixture of sour cream, paint, whipped cream and seafood. Recorded 1987-88 with Tom Herbers, the EP includes "P-9", written for the striking Hormel workers in Austin, Minnesota.

The UK edition added covers of Foreigner and Janis Joplin; the US edition kept only "Chains".

years.cap: Dave Pirner, Dan Murphy, Karl Mueller and Grant Young
years.src: Wikipedia: And the Horse They Rode In On · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: A Keith Richards drummer produces And the Horse They Rode In On
years.p: Steve Jordan, of Richards' X-pensive Winos, cuts most of it live on an A&M soundstage in Los Angeles; it's finished in Cannon Falls, Minnesota.
years.xp: The band mounted a North American tour behind it. The Windsor Star called Murphy's "Gullible's Travels" "one of the best half-dozen rock tracks of the year", and Trouser Press names "Easy Street" "an instant SA anthem".
play: And the Horse They Rode In On

eras.title: Runaway Train
eras.text: A new label, a new producer and a drummer who plays only some of his own record. A ballad Pirner wrote alone on an acoustic guitar goes to No. 5 and wins a Grammy, and the band spends the next decade being asked about it.

years.src: SPIN: Wrong Way on a One-Way Track · Request Magazine, July 1995 · Wikipedia: Grant Young · Wikipedia: Grave Dancers Union
years.h: Michael Beinhorn finds Grant Young's takes lackluster, five songs in
years.p: The producer brings in Sterling Campbell and the two split the drumming, but Campbell is credited only as "percussionist".
years.xp:
Murphy said in SPIN's oral history: "We were all Minneapolis boys...we resisted it." Young says he played on five or six songs. Booker T. Jones cut keyboards in Los Angeles a week after the 1992 riots; Beinhorn says he played on seven songs in five hours.

In Request in July 1995 Pirner said of Young: "Grant, who was my best friend, my drummer for 10 years - I love the guy still." He added: "We didn't have the faith in him that we should've had." Young later ran a Boundary Waters resort near Ely, Minnesota, with his wife Catherine, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Grave Dancers Union · Request Magazine, July 1995
years.h: Grave Dancers Union reaches No. 11 and goes double platinum
years.p: Recorded in three studios with Beinhorn, it also tops the Heatseekers chart; the cover is a 1970 photograph by Jan Saudek.
years.xp: Murphy told Request: "I don't think up until [Grave Dancers Union] we even made a good record." Entertainment Weekly gave it an A and Rolling Stone 3.5 stars, per Wikipedia.

years.h: "Somebody to Shove" sits a week at No. 1 on Modern Rock
years.p: The first single from Grave Dancers Union tops Billboard's chart in a video directed by Zack Snyder.

years.src: SPIN: Wrong Way on a One-Way Track · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
yt: Somebody to Shove, live at the MTV Inaugural Ball
years.h: Bill Clinton gets Soul Asylum at his inauguration
years.p: A few months after "Somebody to Shove" topped the Modern Rock chart, the band plays the MTV Inaugural Ball on Clinton's first inauguration night.
years.xp: SPIN lists En Vogue and Boyz II Men on the same bill, with Dennis Miller hosting. Murphy told SPIN the band also played the White House lawn, and that Clinton was "very funny, charming, and nice" during a 25-minute visit.

years.h: MTV Unplugged puts "Black Gold" on acoustic guitars
years.p: The 1993 set includes the Grave Dancers Union track "Black Gold", which Zack Snyder also directed a video for.

q: It overshadowed everything else we did.
years.src: Guitar Player: Dave Pirner Reveals · Wikipedia: Runaway Train · SPIN: Wrong Way on a One-Way Track · All That's Interesting: Runaway Train
years.h: "Runaway Train" climbs to No. 5 with missing children on screen
years.p: Director Tony Kaye runs photographs of missing children, three versions of 36 faces each, and MTV cuts the on-screen plea for tips over fears it will read as a public service announcement.
years.xp:
Pirner has said he wrote the song around what he now calls undiagnosed depression, on a napkin, after a breakdown over fears of losing his hearing. Guitar Player reports he recorded the acoustic parts on a rented Gibson J-200. The demo, with producer Brian Paulson, was two acoustic guitars and harmony vocals, and the final arrangement barely changed.

All That's Interesting reports Kaye made three versions with 36 children each, using photographs from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. Kaye has said 21 to 26 of them were found, and calls the video "the single most important thing that happened in the history of MTV".

All That's Interesting also notes that several children counted as found had left home on their own, some fleeing abuse, and that not all were glad to see themselves in the video.

years.h: Best Rock Song goes to Pirner for "Runaway Train"
years.p: The 1994 Grammy goes to Dave Pirner as the song's writer, for a band that began as Loud Fast Rules.

eras.title: The hangover
eras.text: Butch Vig produces in Madison, Grant Young is out after ten years, and the follow-up goes platinum without reaching the places Grave Dancers Union did. A benefit prom comes next, then a record that ends the Columbia deal.

years.src: Wikipedia: Let Your Dim Light Shine · Request Magazine, July 1995 · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: Butch Vig produces Let Your Dim Light Shine, and it reaches No. 6
years.p: Recorded at Smart Studios in Madison with Sterling Campbell as full-time drummer; "Misery" hits No. 20 on the Hot 100 and tops Modern Rock.
years.xp:
Pirner told Request: "Making this record was just a bitch, quite frankly." He said the band "really took an easy way out" in dropping Grant Young, who had been drumming for the band for ten years. Trouser Press hears Pirner "straining to sound like himself", and reports critics attacked it as a sellout.

The album went platinum in the US.

years.src: Wikipedia: After the Flood · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: Grand Forks students lose their prom to a flood, so Soul Asylum play one
years.p: The band plays a joint high school prom at Grand Forks Air Force Base for students whose own was cancelled by the Red River flood.
years.xp: The recording came out seven years later as After the Flood: Live from the Grand Forks Prom, June 28, 1997 (Columbia/Legacy, October 5, 2004). It runs 19 tracks, with covers of Smokey Robinson, Marvin Gaye and Alice Cooper, and the back cover shows the burnt-out Security Building, photographed by Eric Hylden for the Grand Forks Herald.

years.src: Wikipedia: Candy from a Stranger · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: Candy from a Stranger stalls at No. 121
years.p: Chris Kimsey produces; "I Will Still Be Laughing" plays over the credits of BASEketball and is the band's last single on Billboard's rock charts.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 2.5 out of 10 and Robert Christgau called it a "dud", per Wikipedia. Wikipedia reports Columbia dropped the band after it underperformed. Ian Mussington was the drummer from 1998 to 2005.

eras.title: For Karl
eras.text: A benefit, a death, and a record finished around a bass player who was not there. Replacements bassist Tommy Stinson and Michael Bland, formerly Prince's drummer, join in late 2005.

years.src: Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: The Quest in Minneapolis throws a benefit for Karl Mueller
years.p: Mueller, diagnosed with throat cancer that May, gets a bill where Bob Mould and [[Grant Hart|571e1aad-0512-45ec-a26d-1d09d786cc53]] play together for the first time in sixteen years.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the Gear Daddies and [[Paul Westerberg|d558f844-4db0-4bc3-ba22-49ad2ca2722e]] on the bill and says the night raised more than $50,000. Mould had produced Soul Asylum's first two records.

years.big: His contribution was always to inspire and to make sure nobody took themselves too seriously.
years.src: Rolling Stone: Soul Asylum's Mueller Dead · AV Club: Interview: Dave Pirner · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: Karl Mueller dies of throat cancer at 41
years.p: That's Dave Pirner on the bassist, in a July 2006 interview. Mueller, a founder since Loud Fast Rules, dies at home; Rolling Stone reports a memorial service at Lakewood Cemetery Chapel.
years.xp: His widow Mary Beth founded the cancer nonprofit Kill Kancer in his memory in 2014, per Wikipedia.

years.big: For me, this record is Karl.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Silver Lining · EnterTheSoulAsylum: Biography · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: The Silver Lining finishes the record Mueller started
years.p: That's Dan Murphy on the band's site. Recorded 2004-06 with John Fields and Steve Hodge, it's the first studio album in eight years; Mueller plays on most tracks and Tommy Stinson and Fields fill in the rest.
years.xp:
ABC and ESPN used "Stand Up and Be Strong" in college football coverage that season, and Prince later covered it on his posthumous 2021 album Welcome 2 America.

Stinson, the Replacements bassist, and Michael Bland, formerly Prince's drummer, joined in late 2005. During Stinson's Guns N' Roses work, George Scot McKelvey and later Pete Donnelly covered bass.

eras.title: Same name, new room
eras.text: Dan Murphy, in since 1981, retires, the bass chair turns over again, and Pirner keeps making records under the name, most recently from Minneapolis after leaving New Orleans.

years.cap: Michael Bland, Dave Pirner and Dan Murphy live in Urbana, Illinois
years.src: Wikipedia: Dan Murphy · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum · Star Tribune: Soul Asylum reacts · EnterTheSoulAsylum: Biography
years.h: Dan Murphy retires after 31 years, weeks after Delayed Reaction
years.p: The album is on 429 Records. Murphy's cousin Justin Sharbono takes his place, and Winston Roye replaces Tommy Stinson on bass.
years.xp:
Murphy's statement said staying in music takes "naivety and swagger. I no longer have either." He donated the Gibson Les Paul he used on every Soul Asylum album to the Minnesota Historical Society and now runs Grapefruit Moon Gallery in Minneapolis. Stinson left over his Guns N' Roses commitments.

Ryan Smith replaced Sharbono in 2016, and Jeremy Tappero has played bass since 2020.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hurry Up and Wait · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum · Please Kill Me: Loud Fast Words
years.h: COVID stops the tour weeks before Hurry Up and Wait comes out
years.p: The twelfth album, made at Nicollet Studios with John Fields, arrives on Blue Élan after Pirner's divorce and move from New Orleans to Minnesota.
years.xp: AllMusic's Mark Deming credits Pirner with a "more pensive and introspective side". The tour stopped in mid-March 2020, and Pirner and Ryan Smith livestreamed through the shutdown. The band played live again on June 26, 2021, opening for the BoDeans in New Lenox, Illinois; the thirteenth album, Slowly but Shirley, followed in 2024.
